title: The 10 Best Rolling Tool Carts
subtitle: Service carts, mechanic carts and power-tool carts for the garage and shop, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A tool cart is an open, rolling shelf unit you push to the job: plastic service carts with deep trays, steel mechanic carts with a locking drawer, and a few specialty carts. If you want a stack of drawers instead, see our rolling tool chests. We ranked 10 best-sellers on rating, review volume and features (locking casters, a lockable drawer, a rust-proof body, storage in the handle and places to hang tools). They run from about $50 for a steel 3-tier cart to $194 for a Rubbermaid commercial cart.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

avoid.name: XCX 3-Tier Heavy Duty Metal Rolling Tool Cart with Drawers, Blue Black
avoid.flag: Sold "with Drawers"; the listing describes none
avoid.verdict: A steel 7-tier cart that costs $58 more than the VEVOR 4-tier, which has a real lockable drawer. The title promises drawers the description never mentions.
reasons: The title says "with Drawers." The bullet points describe three open levels and a pegboard, and never mention a drawer.
It claims 660 lbs, more than the Rubbermaid commercial cart (500 lbs), from a 40.8 lb steel cart, with no per-shelf rating.
At $129.99 it costs more than every steel cart on this page. The VEVOR 4-tier ($72.18) and Pelnuies ($49.99) both have a lockable drawer.

buyers_guide.a: A cart is open shelves you push to the job, so everything is in reach while you work. A chest is a stack of drawers that keeps tools organized and locked away. Many shops have both: a chest for storage and a cart for the job in front of them.

Polypropylene and structural-foam carts don't rust, dent or chip, and they're quieter. Steel carts usually add a lockable drawer and pegboard sides, but the paint can chip and the steel can rust in a damp garage.

buyers_guide.q: How much weight do I need?
buyers_guide.a: Most service carts here are rated for 500 to 550 lbs total, which covers tools, parts and a small compressor. Check whether the rating is per shelf or total, and load the bottom shelf heaviest so the cart doesn't tip.
If you work on a sloped garage floor or lean on the cart, yes. A cart without brakes can roll away while you're working. Several carts here list braking casters; the WEN and MaxWorks don't.

buyers_guide.q: What size casters should I get?
buyers_guide.a: Five-inch casters roll over cords, cracks and expansion joints much more easily than small 3-inch wheels. Non-marring or rubber-wrapped wheels are quieter and won't scuff floors.
